newsitem.title: CHINA: China chamber calls for payment of accepted bills.
newsitem.headline: China chamber calls for payment of accepted bills.

text.p: China's International Chamber of Commerce has appealed to the Supreme People's Court to stop banks from refusing to pay accepted bills to foreign companies, the China Daily Business Weekly said on Sunday.

The chamber, ICC China, had noted increasingly vocal complaints from foreign firms that Chinese banks failed to pay accepted bills where there were disputes over import contracts, the official newspaper said.

The practice was "seriously undercutting the reliability of letters of credit in trade with China", and damaging the credit rating of domestic banks, it quoted the chamber as saying in its appeal to the Supreme Court.
The court could give a judicial explanation ordering local courts to separate contract disputes from letter of credit payment, said ICC China executive secretary Li Haifeng.

In 1989, the court ruled that payment of letters of credit, especially of accepted bills, could not be frozen unless cheating was discovered within a reasonable period, the newspaper quoted him as saying. It gave no details.
The newspaper did not say when the court was expected to decide on the appeal.
